target_customer: Clients seeking vetted mobile and app designers, and designers seeking work
problem: Finding a good mobile designer was hard on open contest marketplaces; Scoutzie offered a curated community vetted by portfolio.
business_model: Curated marketplace taking a fee on design projects; later experiments with other models

founders.name: Kirill Zubovsky
founders.background_notes: On the YC page and TechCrunch. His current site presents him as a YC alum running a product building service.

founders.name: Jaigouk Kim
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page only.

founders.name: Jennifer Toda
founders.background_notes: Named with Zubovsky as founder in TechCrunch, August 2012; not on the YC page.

exit.reason: CB Insights says the team tried several models and decided in 2015 to shut the product down.

competitors.name: 99designs
competitors.traction_then: Called the most obvious competitor by TechCrunch

competitors.name: Fjord
competitors.what: Design agency the founders compared themselves to

competitors.name: Happy Cog
competitors.what: Design agency the founders compared themselves to

technical_complexity.rationale: A portfolio site with curation and a proposal workflow; standard web engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Curated designer supply was the asset, but designers could list elsewhere and clients could go direct.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent response is documented; the team tried several models and closed the product in 2015 per CB Insights.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in August 2012 described demand for vetted mobile design as app building boomed, though no revenue or customer figures were published.

branding.domain_note: scoutzie.com is still held by the founder and now advertises a product building service.

identity.voice_and_tone: Curated and selective, framed around scouting designers by portfolio

branding.brand_signature: Chief Scout title for the founder and scouting of designers

brand_strength.rationale: Covered by TechCrunch, TNW and GeekWire at launch; the scouting theme was coherent but no sources show community pull.

outcome_analysis: Scoutzie launched in 2012 as a curated mobile designer marketplace backed by YC, 500 Startups and SV Angel, tried several business models and shut the product in 2015 according to CB Insights. The founder now sells product building services under the same domain. The failure codes reflect model experimentation without a durable fit; the exact reason is not stated by the company.
notes: CB Insights says $20K raised over 3 rounds; seed in June 2012 with Y Combinator and Steve Blank rests on that single database, amount not itemised. The August 2012 round entry records the TechCrunch backer list without an amount or confirmed stage, hence stage other. The failure factors are inferred from CB Insights language about changing models, not a company statement. A wip.co comment refers to Scoutzie 2.0 in 2025 and the YC directory still marks the company Inactive.
